purpose: Boy clothing mesh material; original head, silhouette and identity retained.
prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create a new four-part clothing texture atlas for the small boy in this painterly side-scrolling game. Reference image is costume/style continuity ONLY. Keep the original worn slate/teal short wool jacket and muted olive-brown trousers; preserve this quiet, humble costume. NO heads, faces, hair, hands, feet or new character design. Genuine transparent background. Square 1536x1536 or larger with four isolated cloth pieces in a spacious2x2 grid and broad transparent gutters. Top left: short child jacket torso only, no arms, worn collar, simple small buttons, deep teal/slate grey wool, broad naturally shaded folds; full opaque front cloth without large empty holes, straight-on side-profile-friendly flattened clothing shape. Top right: separate upper sleeve cloth patch in matching wool, broad soft shoulder/arm folds rather than thin stripes. Bottom left: separate forearm sleeve with simple cuff, matching wool, generous naturally bent fabric wrinkles and no hand. Bottom right: isolated muted olive-brown trouser/knee fabric panel with worn softly folded cloth, no foot. All material interiors opaque and generous for mesh UV sampling; high-resolution finely painted but simple broad forms readable at game scale. Hand-painted oil/gouache materials matching the reference, warm soft rim/top-left light with cool soft fill, open midtones and visible fabric. No outlines, logos, extra accessories, boots, backgrounds, cast shadows, text, mannequins or plastic/CGI. Original identity and palette must stay consistent.
integration: Original generated RGBA retained without raster modifications; runtime atlas regions and deforming meshes use these pixels; mipmaps enabled.
